item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: Two graphs for the comparison of age structure between country x and country y. The x axis of both graphs shows percent of population, 0 to 8 percent, and the y-axis of both graphs is age, from 0 to 89. Each graph shows males and females separately, though the age structure is the same. Each graph indicates the proportion that are age 0 to 19, who are going to have children, those who are age 20 to 44, who are having children, and those age 45 to 89, who have finished having children. Country x age distribution shows rapid growth, where the younger ages are a greater percentage of the population than those who are older. Country y shows slow growth, where the older ages are an equal or greater percentage of the population than those who are younger. Country X has a larger percentage of people in the “having children” or “going to have children” categories than does country Y.]

The graphs for Country X and Country Y show the age structure of each country’s population. The population is divided into three age groups from youngest to oldest. The graphs enable predictions about population growth.

B. Why could Country Y expect to have a bigger problem taking care of its elderly population than Country X?

descriptors: Within Country Y, there is a relatively larger population of elderly people (“finished having children”) compared with younger populations.
Incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

item.scoring_notes:
Note: The comparison between older and younger people must be made or implied.
Country X and Country Y do not have to be mentioned.
Examples: More older people than younger people
Not enough young people to take care of the elderly
Less number of people “having children” to keep up the population
Aging population, less youngsters, lesser workforce

Examples: There are many more elders in Y than X
Country Y has a wider range of not having children than country X
item.figure_description:
Two population pyramid graphs side by side under the heading "Comparison of Age Structure Between Country X and Country Y". Both graphs have a vertical axis on the left labeled "Ages" with tick marks from 0 to 89 in increments of 5 (0, 4, 9, 14, 19, 24, 29, 34, 39, 44, 49, 54, 59, 64, 69, 74, 79, 84, 89). A central vertical line divides "Males" on the left from "Females" on the right. The horizontal axis at the bottom is labeled "Percent of Population" with tick marks numbered 8 down to 0 on the left side and 0 up to 8 on the right side.

The left graph is subtitled "Country X Age Distribution / Rapid Growth". It forms a wide-based pyramid. The base (age 0) extends to approximately 7% on both the male and female sides. At age 19, it is about 3% on each side. At age 44, it is about 1.5% on each side, tapering to 0% at age 89.

The right graph is subtitled "Country Y Age Distribution / Slow Growth". It has a much narrower base and more vertical sides. At age 0, it extends to about 3% for males and 3% for females. At age 19, it is slightly below 3% on each side. At age 44, it is about 2% on each side, tapering to 0% at age 89.

Below the graphs is a key with three boxes:
- A solid dark gray box labeled "Ages 0–19 Going to have children", corresponding to the shaded bottom section (ages 0 to 19) in both graphs.
- An unshaded white box labeled "Ages 20–44 Having children", corresponding to the unshaded middle section (ages 20 to 44) in both graphs.
- A diagonally hatched box labeled "Ages 45–89 Finished having children", corresponding to the hatched top section (ages 45 to 89) in both graphs.

reference_items.stem:
The graph shows the distribution of crops grown in a certain country.

[Image: Pie chart showing the distribution of crops]

According to the information in the graph, which of these statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: More oats are grown than wheat.

options.label: B
options.text: Corn is more than one-half of the country’s crop.

options.label: C
options.text: Oats are more than one-third of the country’s crop.

options.label: D
options.text: The total crop of oats and wheat is greater than the corn crop.

reference_items.figure_description:
A pie chart showing four sectors labeled with crop types:
- 'Corn': occupies slightly less than half of the circle, spanning from the 12 o'clock position clockwise to approximately the 4:30 position (roughly 135° to 140°).
- 'Oats': adjacent clockwise from Corn, spanning from approximately 4:30 to 7 o'clock (roughly 75°).
- 'Other': adjacent clockwise from Oats, spanning from approximately 7 o'clock to 8 o'clock (roughly 30°).
- 'Wheat': adjacent clockwise from Other to Corn, spanning from approximately 8 o'clock to 12 o'clock (roughly 115° to 120°).

reference_items.stem:
[Image: A numbered axis, from 0 to 2. Two dots are shown, “P” and “Q”. “P” lies roughly halfway between 0 and 1 and “Q” lies roughly three fourths between 0 and 1.]

P and Q represent two fractions on the number line above.

P × Q = N.

Which of these shows the location of N on the number line?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: A numbered axis from 0 to 2 where “P” lies roughly halfway between 0 and 1, “Q” lays roughly three fourths between 0 and 1, and “N” lies halfway between 1 and 2.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: A numbered axis from 0 to 2 where “P” lies roughly halfway between 0 and 1, “Q” lies roughly three fourths between 0 and 1, and “N” lies after Q but before 1.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: A numbered axis from 0 to 2 where “P” lies roughly halfway between 0 and 1, “Q” lies roughly three fourths between 0 and 1, and “N” lies in between P and Q.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: A numbered axis from 0 to 2 where “P” lies roughly halfway between 0 and 1, “Q” lies roughly three fourths between 0 and 1, and “N” lies in between 0 and P.]

reference_items.figure_description:
The figure above the text shows a horizontal number line with an arrow at the right end. There are tick marks labeled 0, 1, and 2, with equal spacing between 0 and 1 and between 1 and 2. Between 0 and 1, two points are marked with black dots: point P is labeled below the line at approximately 0.5 (halfway between 0 and 1), and point Q is labeled below the line at approximately 0.75 (three-fourths of the distance from 0 to 1).

Each of the four response options shows the same number line with points P and Q in their original positions, along with a third point labeled N above the line:
- Option A: Point N is marked halfway between 1 and 2, at approximately 1.5.
- Option B: Point N is marked between Q and 1, at approximately 0.85.
- Option C: Point N is marked between P and Q, at approximately 0.625.
- Option D: Point N is marked between 0 and P, at approximately 0.25.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A large triangle. The left angle is 45 degrees and the top angle is 65 degrees. A line is drawn on the side between the 45 and 64 degree angle to form two smaller triangles—one adjacent to the larger triangle, and one contained within the larger triangle. The right most angle of the triangle adjacent to the larger triangle has an angle of 30 degrees. The smaller triangle contained within the bigger triangle has an angle x that is formed by the right side of the triangle and the drawn line.]

In the figure above, what is the value of x?
reference_items.figure_description: A geometric figure featuring intersecting lines and triangles. A triangle has a horizontal base, a left side with an interior angle of 45° at the bottom-left vertex, and an interior angle of 65° at the top vertex. A line segment extends from the top vertex down to the base. A second line segment extends from a point on the left side of the triangle down and to the right, crossing the first line segment and ending at the rightmost endpoint of the extended horizontal base, where the interior angle is labeled 30°. Near the top vertex, a smaller triangle is bounded by the upper part of the left side, the upper part of the segment from the top vertex, and the crossing segment; the interior angle at the intersection of the two segments is marked with an arc and labeled x.

- White box: Cherry Cola
- Solid black box: Lemon Cola

- 1999: Cherry Cola bar reaches 20; Lemon Cola bar reaches 45.
- 2000: Cherry Cola bar reaches 30; Lemon Cola bar reaches 50.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
